newsitem.title: USA: QUEIROZ LEAVING METROSTARS FOR GRAMPUS EIGHT IN JAPAN.
newsitem.headline: QUEIROZ LEAVING METROSTARS FOR GRAMPUS EIGHT IN JAPAN.

text.p: Carlos Queiroz will quit coaching the New York/New Jersey MetroStars at the end of the Major League Soccer season to become coach of the Grampus Eight of Japan's J-League, the MLS team said Monday.
Queiroz, the former Portuguese national team coach, will succeed Frenchman Arsene Wegner, who left the Grampus Eight to coach Arsenal in the English Premier League.

"The offer from Japan was extremely lucrative," said MetroStars general manager Charlie Stillitano, "and while we were able to make a substantial offer ourselves, in the end we could not compete financially with Grampus Eight and the J-League."

The 43-year-old Queiroz was brought on in midseason to replace Eddie Firmani and bolster the struggling MetroStars, who have a 14-16 record and can clinch a playoff berth with a regulation win over the Columbus Crew on Wednesday.
Under Queiroz, the third-place MetroStars are 11-11.
"I cannot give any negative reasons for leaving, but it is a new challenge and I think I must take the new challenge," Queiroz told reporters.

Queiroz is reportedly getting a two-year deal worth $4 million from Grampus Eight. The MetroStars countered with an offer of $500,000-a-year over three years, which would have made Queiroz the highest paid coach in U.S. soccer history.
"The timing is bad because Wednesday is the biggest game of the year," Stillitano said. "All we can do is go forward from here."
Queiroz, who guided Portugal to a pair of FIFA youth championships, was fired as coach of Sporting Lisbon earlier this year.
